notes.title: London Overground Suffragette line - Coming Soon!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/bc69a8f507f5c1345c8b5efd6882b9365797ded9.jpg[/img]

It’s time to go Overground on the latest London line to come to Train Sim World. Get ready for an Aventra adventure in Train Sim World 4: London Overground Suffragette line: Gospel Oak – Barking Riverside, arriving 19th March!

[h3][b]The Route: Gospel Oak – Barking Riverside[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/414e333b1119fcbbad858a8b6bb936c2378f61b1.png[/img]

150 years in the making; the Gospel Oak to Barking Line was happenstance-constructed through the means of multiple companies building adjacent lines. As links, junctions and various termini were built and changed, this meandering route through no less than 7 of North & East London’s boroughs took shape as a vital strategic railway.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/8cd2006b77bf16164ec2b84347c3d93b4dec6818.jpg[/img]

Once earmarked for closure, and allowed to be rundown into disarray, Transport for London (TfL) took the line under their wing alongside other routes in 2007 when London Overground was launched to transform them into lines fit for the future. State-of-the-art throughout, the line from Gospel Oak is now an electrified, high density passenger route, making use of the brand-new Class 710 Aventra, while also still leaving space for freight as part of the National Rail network.

Having spent years with an avid community following, the route became affectionately known as the ‘GOBLIN’, a portmanteau of Gospel Oak - Barking Line.[url=https://live.dovetailgames.com/live/train-sim-world/articles/article/tfl-new-name-overground-route][b] But from February 2024 it was announced that the route would be known the Suffragette line[/b][/url] as part of TfL plans to name all of the London Overground routes to make the network easier for customers to navigate. Once rebranding is complete later this year it will be known as the Suffragette line, in recognition of how the early 20th century working-class movement in the East End, paved the way for women’s rights – empowering women to have a significant impact on society, in the past, present and will continue to do in the future.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/dfa4969489a90fd5c5a21050791012981cdd4c26.jpg[/img]

The in-game route has scenery that represents the built-up area around this part of north London, including dense collections of residential buildings and lighting that recreates the suburban atmosphere after the sun has gone down.

A dedicated team of route builders have put a lot of effort into unique scenery assets on the route, including the two distinctive stations at Barking and Barking Riverside. The former being a large interchange station for other London lines and the latter being a brand-new station in anticipation of the riverside development that is very much under way.

As well as the standard route maps, our route builders have had a lot of fun hiding 25 Goblins around the route, in reference to the informal name given to this line by locals and enthusiasts. Some of these have been placed in some difficult-to-find locations, making them a little more challenging than typical route collectibles!

[h3][b]New EMU: London Overground Class 710 Aventra[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/5289386ee7cd070758ee29c668ac14c69751ab70.jpg[/img]

One of the latest trains in TfL’s fleet comes to Train Sim World in the form of the Class 710 Aventra. Introduced in 2019, these sleek and modern electric multiple units replaced older stock and have variants running under other operators throughout Greater London, including the Class 345 units on the Elizabeth Line.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/98d6ff60987e6cd69c776274baa6c93f8fb17bc0.jpg[/img]

In-game, the interiors will be familiar to London commuters and tourists alike with relevant signage and PIS displays present, as well as the distinctive moquette found on the seating.

In the cab, the experience is very much dominated by the use of screens, with no analogue dials in sight! Players looking for the window blinds will need to find the button for it, as these are operated by a switch rather than by hand. Like the Thameslink Class 700 loco Add-on, the Class 710 supports dual voltage functionality for use on routes with third rail electricity in Free Roam.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/ea5a10e34b9d459d44eab182d6ff2bc40746d6c8.jpg[/img]

Due to the way in which the game treats third and fourth rail power on the Train Sim World Compatible route Add-on Bakerloo Line, players wanting to drive the Class 710 on that route will need to enable Scenario Planner’s ‘Off the Rails Mode’.

[h3][b]Services, layers and Gameplay[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/fdf2335f2651bc8915e7733142c084556572f3df.jpg[/img]

Up to four trains per hour (tph) run along this line between Gospel Oak and Barking Riverside resulting in 154 playable services for the Class 710 in and amongst a total of over 1,000 services when factoring in AI and layers from other pieces of content. Timekeeping will be important throughout each service run, as will stopping points with trains fitting snug into the length of some platforms.

Freight services will be available to the vast majority of Train Sim World 4 players as these will layer in from the East Coast Main Line Class 66 and FKA wagons, though other Class 66 variants (including from recently released Gameplay Packs) will be available to select for those that own that content. Additional freight using other forms of rolling stock will also layer in such as those from Southeastern Highspeed.

Other playable service layers include the RHTT from the Train Sim World Compatible Loco Add-on Bundle, as well as both diesel and steam rail tour services from other Train Sim World route Add-ons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/bda8c520e1223deb77f102510d9ee669cf6b36f7.jpg[/img]

Between Crouch End and Harringay, the line crosses the East Coast Main Line, where players will glimpse passing LNER Class 801 Azuma services in the form of AI traffic utilising the full ECML timetable. Other AI services present include the Thameslink Class 700, Flying Scotsman and a 1938 Underground Stock rail tour for players with the relevant content.

There are also some sneaky Easter Egg AI services that players may spot throughout the route, similar to those found on Southeastern Highspeed. We’ll let you enjoy hunting those down for yourselves...

The majority of AI traffic is formed of additional Class 710 London Overground services utilising parts of other Overground lines that run under, over or join with the Gospel Oak – Barking line. This includes a short section of the Lea Valley Cheshunt / Enfield Town Line that crosses perpendicular to the Suffragette line between South Tottenham and Blackhorse Road.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/32b881cea3d3609c49cd4298b2f29cdedf05b26a.jpg[/img]

Scenarios are centred around various special events throughout the year, with players having to negotiate specific operations for Hallowe’en and Bonfire Night, as well as busy football fixtures and weather-related disruption.

[b]Train Sim World 4: London Overground Suffragette line: Gospel Oak – Barking Riverside[/b] route Add-on will be available from 19th March for Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Epic Games Store, and Steam for [b]£24.99/€29.99/$29.99[/b]

Join the Railfan TV team on [b][url=https://www.twitch.tv/trainsimworldofficial]Twitch[/url][/b] and [b][url=https://www.youtube.com/user/RailSimulatorDotCom]YouTube[/url][/b] at 19:00 UTC on March 14th for a preview of Train Sim World 4: London Overground Suffragette line: Gospel Oak – Barking Riverside.

notes.title: Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim - Out Now!
notes.content:
[h3]Dramatic mountains, cross-border action and a classic tap-changer locomotive all arrive today with Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim![/h3]

[previewyoutube=1jtWZunncek;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Scenarios Update[/h2]

You may have seen earlier this week that we had identified a few issues with Scenarios on the route which affected the pre-order period for Steam players.

We are pleased to report that the issues, related to completing Scenarios, have been resolved. Players on Steam and Epic will be able to play all 5 Scenarios from launch.

PlayStation and Xbox players should receive an update later today, which will add in the fifth scenario for the route.

[h2]The Route: Salzburg – Rosenheim [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/0ae342b93b681bd5d96a401ab241a1d7c1341ce1.jpg[/img]

With origins from as early as 1828, the Rosenheim – Salzburg railway has ferried passengers and freight through Bavaria and across into Austria for many decades. Fast forward to 2013, when this route Add-on is set, and these services are being hauled by electric locomotives of varying types.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/66c9082eae249c4cbaaed5248f282670be4bb19b.jpg[/img]

In the distance, the landscape is overlooked by mountainous terrain which has been worked on by our environment teams to create a beautiful backdrop for the stations along the line, together with architecture that’s representative of the local Bavarian culture. Along the line side, players will need to hunt down trees that need cutting up and forming into log piles as part of this release’s route collectibles. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/ccd281a5be799641cc4ce959b3f1d764d69fd785.jpg[/img]

Our launch trailer already hints at Salzburg’s most famous musician, with the city being the birthplace of Mozart and being a filming location for The Sound Of Music. A number of stations in this important Austria city lie within its limits, including the Salzburg Liefering station which at the time was still under construction. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/0e95b98a753a5667ec72a493172596824a615b2c.jpg[/img]

Salzburg Hbf is populated with trains from Austrian operator ÖBB, as well as the visiting DB trains, making for a truly multi-national atmosphere. As with other Train Sim World 4 routes, there are some populated shops and cafes within the station, dioramas of workers discussing construction and in this route Add-on there are even working lifts for players to use as they get around.

[h2]Locomotives, Rolling Stock and base timetable [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/b577b8418e78ce5188960e1aee1f284a9614008f.jpg[/img]

[b]Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim can be experienced in a number of ways with three forms of traction included in the route Add-on. These include:[/b]

[b](NEW) DB BR 111[/b] – An electric locomotive from the 1970s that is still used today, featuring tap-changer controls and a distinctive horn. Eastbound services from Rosenheim to Salzburg have the DB BR 111 leading the train.

[b]Gen 4 Dosto coaches[/b] – heading up push-pull westbound services out of Salzburg towards Rosenheim. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/8d1d6ffde3074d03fb3b98981e1e2d056ef1dc18.jpg[/img]

[b]DB BR 185.2[/b] - A modern electric locomotive rostered for freight duty with Habbiins and Sggmrss Wagons. These mostly run end-to-end services, with other freight stock substituting some services for players than own other route Add-ons.

[b]ÖBB 4024 Talent 1[/b] – An EMU run by Austrian operator ÖBB for local services in and out of Salzburg Hbf. These run between Salzburg and Freilassing to off-world destinations including: Schwarzach-St.Veit, Golling-Abtenau, Saalfelden, Wels, Bad Reichenhall, and Berchtesgaden.

[h2]Additional Service Layers [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/c6b164728e1c0972b2afcdb847bb88eb0762ce84.jpg[/img]

[b]Additional playable and AI timetable services appear for players that own other German route and locomotive Add-ons. These include:[/b]

[list]
[*] [b]DB BR 628.2[/b], in red DB livery ([b]Niddertalbahn[/b] required) - these come from off-world locations such as Landshut or Mühldorf to operate between Freilassing and Salzburg or from Waging to operate between Hufschlag and Traunstein.
[*] [b]DB BR 101 loco Add-on[/b] – these operate IC, EC, EN and CNL services using the 101 and IC coaches.
[*] [b]DB BR 103[/b] rail tour with heritage InterCity train (Linke Rheinstrecke required)
[*] [b]Railpool BR 193 Vectron[/b] and Eanos Wagon
[*] [b]DB BR 363[/b], in red DB livery (loco Add-on required)
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/519ce4ffe37f89a043ef934c1100408436134250.jpg[/img]

[b]Further AI and Static services from other Train Sim World Add-ons consist of the following:[/b]

[list]
[*] [b]DB BR 628.2[/b] can be seen at Freilassing, Traunstein, Prien and Rosenheim
[*] [b]DB BR 425[/b] at Traunstein
[*] [b]ICE 3[/b] can be seen at Bahnhof Rosenheim
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/3c22addc4a5663aed94781c9c6f97cf4008ece4f.jpg[/img]

[h3]At Freilassing, a number of static museum exhibits for players with Linke Rheinstrecke or Ruhr Sieg Nord can be seen, including:[/h3]

[list]
[*] [b]DB BR 103[/b] which will appear between the months of March to August
[*] [b]DB BR 110[/b] which will appear between the months of December to February
[*] [b]DB BR 155[/b] which will appear between the months of September to November
[/list]

In anticipation of the forthcoming [b]Semmeringbahn: Wiener Neustadt – Mürzzuschlag[/b] route Add-on there will also be 4 playable EC services that use the [b]ÖBB 1116[/b] electric locomotive and coaches for players that own that route. These coaches will also be seen as static stock at Salzburg Hbf.

If you missed our preview stream, head over to Twitch and YouTube and join the Railfan TV Team to see Train Sim World 4: Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim in action. 

[previewyoutube=PqCA1FVQrMo;full][/previewyoutube]

Train Sim World 4: Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim route Add-on is out now for €35.99/£29.99/$39.99

Find out more about Train Sim World 4 by following @trainsimworld on [url=https://twitter.com/trainsimworld]X/Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/trainsim/]Instagram[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/trainsimworld/]Facebook[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/RailSimulatorDotCom]YouTube[/url], [url=https://www.twitch.tv/trainsimworldofficial]Twitch[/url], and [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@trainsimworldofficial]TikTok[/url].

notes.title: Train Sim World 4 Game Update - February 26th
notes.content:
Good morning everyone,

Alongside our preparation for the release of Salzburg-Rosenheim tomorrow, we have a patch going live today which brings a small range of improvements to address various issues, including a set of achievements not unlocking on PlayStation and Xbox platforms, fixes for Formation Designer UI-related issues and an improvement to correct the GWE HST power car in Livery Designer.

These will be rolling out to players on all platforms over the course of the next 24 hours – [i]Steam platforms should start to receive these updates, with consoles coming later.[/i]

[h3][b]Headliners[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] Fixed a range of achievements not unlocking across various console platforms
[*] Fixed an issue where the GWE HST had the incorrect power car livery in Livery Designer.
[*] Additional fixes to UI issues for Formation Designer
[/list]

[h3][b]Full Changelog[/b][/h3]
[b]Core[/b]
[list]
[*] Removed incorrect entry on the ‘My Trains’ tab for “GWR HST Mk3 TFD”
[*] Fixed various instances of unlocalised loco names in menus.
[*] Fixed an issue where the awarded medal would incorrectly scroll with text when shown on scenario completion screens.
[/list]

[b]Achievements[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with the [b]MSB: Clean Sweep[/b] achievement not unlocking on PS5.
[*] Fixed an issue with the [b]RRO: Top of the Class[/b] achievement not unlocking on PS5.
[*] Fixed an issue with the [b]RRO: Wupper Wonderer[/b] achievement not unlocking on PS5.
[*] Fixed an issue with the [b]LGV: A Great Triumph[/b] achievement not unlocking on PS5.
[*] Fixed an issue with the [b]Maintalbahn: Desiro-able[/b] achievement not unlocking on PS4 & PS5.
[*] Fixed an issue with the [b]PBO: Pace Yourself[/b] achievement not unlocking across Xbox platforms.
[/list]

[b]Livery Designer[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where the GWE HST had the incorrect power car livery.
[*] Fixed various issues with the visuals for UI buttons being distorted on PS5
[/list]

[b]Formation Designer[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where duplicated vehicles could be shown in Formation Designer menus.
[*] Fixed gradient rating not updating when adding rolling stock.
[*] Fixed 'Total Weight' value being incorrect in the formation stats.
[*] Fixed formation name not saving when changing it via Formation Editor settings.
[*] Fixed an issue where the LMS 8F Stanier loco fails to be displayed. In Formation Designer Menus.
[*] Fixed the Copy shortcut icon which was showing greyed out on some occasions incorrectly, now operates correctly duplicating the current item of stock.
[*] Fixed the Up/Down shortcut button which was permanently greyed out, now works and allows items of stock to be repositioned in the consist.
[*] Fixed the Options/Copy button which did not work at all, does the same as the short cut by duplicating the current item of stock.
[/list]

[b]Scenario Planner[/b]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue where an assigned formation was not being displayed if multiple services existed.
[/list]

Thank you for your patience, let us know of any feedback following the patch! :)

notes.title: Bahnstrecke Salzburg–Rosenheim - Pre-order on Steam!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/ecfb2461a85c5ace3ae1b72cf4438394b6ee8b6a.jpg[/img]

It’s time to cross borders again in Train Sim World! But this time the balance has shifted. Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim runs mostly through beautiful Bavarian countryside on German rails before entering one of Austria’s most important cities.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2584130/Train_Sim_World_4_Bahnstrecke_Salzburg__Rosenheim_Route_AddOn/

[h3][b]Watch our Rosenheim Preview Livestream[/b][/h3]

[previewyoutube=PqCA1FVQrMo;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Locomotives and Rolling Stock[/h2]

[h3]DB BR 111 + Gen 4 Dosto coaches[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/773b487e6dd500fc37dde22151525429dab6ae00.jpg[/img]

After a brief dip into the diesel world with our previous route Add-on Maintalbahn, we’re back to all-electric services and a brand-new electric locomotive to Train Sim World – DB’s BR 111. This ageing classic from the 70s and 80s features a tap changer control system with both manual and semi-automatic input. Unlike the DB BR 103 however (seen in the Linke Rheinstrecke route Add-on), the cab of this locomotive doesn’t have a wheel, but lever controls instead.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/b30c4906f374d1483925e1c551d883d25a49d713.jpg[/img]

In reality, the DB BR 111 has seen service across a variety of German routes, including use on S-Bahn services and hauling InterCity trains. In Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim these locomotives haul Gen 4 Dosto coaches across the full length of the route as push-pull operations, with the cab car leading the way on return journeys.

As well as the tap changer controls, there are some unique features to note, including the pantograph and the recognisable horn.

[h3]ÖBB 4024 Talent 1 EMU[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/3dd307d3f5af434e7af9c7fb3d08cf878e0d9a8d.jpg[/img]

In and around Salzburg Hbf, ÖBB services will feature the 4024 Talent 1 EMU previously seen in S-Bahn Vorarlberg. This low-floor, stop-start commuter railcar is ideal for cross-border services, with variants of it used all across Europe. Its inclusion will fill out some of the platforms at Salzburg Hbf and add a different style of operation to tackle across part of the route.

The ÖBB 4024 Talent 1 EMU is included with Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim. Players do not need to own S-Bahn Vorarlberg to make use of this train.

[h3]DB BR 185.2 + Habbiins, Sggmrss Wagons[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/68476b0698c92b06cdd1db1b341fb4701dd7c467.jpg[/img]

It’s not all about passenger services though. Also included is the DB BR 185.2 electric locomotive, previously seen in a number of route Add-ons, to provide freight service operations. Players wanting to enjoy the route with some familiar traction will no doubt relish the opportunity to operate the more modern 185 in new surroundings. Services consists of end-to-end runs with both the Habbiins and Sggmrss Wagons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/6038c7fef79ab9a61f876e1a41d4ff6890972baa.jpg[/img]

Other wagons will also substitute into freight services from other route and loco Add-ons for players that own them.

The DB BR 185.2 is included with Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim. Players do not need to own any previous route Add-ons to make use of this locomotive.

[h2]The Route: Salzburg – Rosenheim[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/1ad6202c3dd96dc0852e6b696cff16e525eadae8.jpg[/img]

Our continuation into Austria for Train Sim World 4 may only be a short stretch at the eastern end of this route, but it’s an important one. Beyond Salzburg, the rest of the 89km route runs through Germany’s Bavaria region.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/9330841c8bab57434b47cb7fb9a7bead7c440fca.jpg[/img]

Salzburg has long been one of the most important cities in Austria with a vast amount of cultural and railway history. It is the birthplace of famed composer Mozart, who continues to influence the music world today, including our tease trailer!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/858b5cc6edabeffbf99e006fcd0e557912f813bd.jpg[/img]

The line out to Rosenheim has origins from 1828 and took many years of theorising, designing, and funding to construct. The first station at Rosenheim was opened originally in 1857 but after the opening of the line to Salzburg was superseded by a station on the current site. This new station received alterations and repairs over time, including after war damage and the current Bahnhof Rosenheim was inaugurated in 1957. The original station now serves as the town hall, or Rathaus.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/c5ce82ec05f47201e28e4b83bb073f232e3b6a3a.jpg[/img]

Along the route, the scenic countryside delights drivers and passengers alike with sights of the Bavaria region, including the area around the Chiemsee lake.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/66c9082eae249c4cbaaed5248f282670be4bb19b.jpg[/img]

Distant mountains create a stunning backdrop for most of the route, with bridges and viaducts present at various points along the line. The distinctive vernacular of this region’s buildings and stations is also apparent. Thirteen stations over 89km of track include towns and villages in the Bavarian hills, such as Übersee, Bernau am Chiemsee and Teisendorf. Some stations now have working lifts that the player can use to explore!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/790bcf268b31b1529a5d9c4e76f104929c131bb6.jpg[/img]

Players will be able to find collectibles along the way, including the staple route maps and first aid kits seen on other routes, as well as lovely flowers and logs which need cutting up along the line side.

[h3]Services, Layers and Gameplay[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/57b2b7d1cbcfed1ebf75c5f9a25712bc5f277018.jpg[/img]

Eastbound passenger services from Rosenheim to Salzburg will be headed by the DB BR 111, with westbound services operated via the Dosto cab car. Westbound München Hbf services will then travel off the map at Rosenheim.

The DB BR 111 will also no doubt form a popular Free Roam choice for players with other German route Add-ons such as Dresden – Riesa and Köln - Aachen.

ÖBB 4024 services can be operated between Salzburg and Freilassing with their final destinations being off the map stations including: Schwarzach-St.Veit, Golling-Abtenau, Saalfelden, Wels, Bad Reichenhall and Berchtesgaden.

There will also be depot moves at Freilassing and Rosenheim.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/641ebf81194b7d0eb75cc3bf9d4f2a8433ed7a67.jpg[/img]

Service layers and substitutions from other owned Add-ons feature a variety of different operations and locomotives, including:
[list]
[*] [b]DB BR 628.2[/b], in red DB livery (Niddertalbahn)
[*] [b]DB BR 101[/b] loco Add-on
[*] [b]DB BR 103[/b] rail tour with heritage InterCity train (Linke Rheinstrecke)
[*] [b]Railpool BR 193 Vectron[/b] and Eanos Wagon
[*] [b]DB BR 363[/b], in red DB livery (loco Add-on required)
[/list]

If you caught our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HL8rA-45C6w][b]Dovetail Direct event[/b][/url] you’ll also know that we’re working on a fully Austrian route Add-on with Semmeringbahn: Wiener Neustadt – Mürzzuschlag. We’ll have more to discuss on that later down the line, but upon release, the ÖBB 1116 locomotive will also layer into Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim.

Train Sim World 4: Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim route Add-on will be available from 27th February for Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Epic Games Store, and Steam for [b]€35.99/£29.99/$39.99[/b]

Find out more about Train Sim World 4 by following @trainsimworld on [b][url=https://twitter.com/trainsimworld]Twitter[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.instagram.com/trainsim/]Instagram[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.facebook.com/trainsimworld]Facebook[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.youtube.com/user/RailSimulatorDotCom]YouTube[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.twitch.tv/trainsimworldofficial]Twitch[/url][/b], and [b][url=https://www.tiktok.com/@trainsimworldofficial]TikTok[/url][/b].

notes.title: Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim, Coming Soon!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=DDtrqVC9lh8;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3]A new locomotive joins the DB roster on more cross-border services between German and Austria. Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim is coming 27th February![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/1fd4a41cfa6cf19cde8e6ca1c0c8114d3adbd7de.jpg[/img]

If you caught [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HL8rA-45C6w]our Dovetail Direct event[/url] this month, you’ll have seen announcements for our next Train Sim World routes and locomotives and a few teases of content that’s coming a little further down the line.

One such route was our next cross-border offering: [b]Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim[/b], featuring the [b]DB BR 111 electric locomotive[/b]. In anticipation of its release, we’d thought we show some more screenshots of the stunning Bavarian countryside and some of the thirteen stations featured.

[i][b]Steam players will be able to pre-order this route from 1800 UTC Tuesday 20th February with a 10% discount.[/b][/i]

It will release on all platforms on [b]Tuesday 27th February[/b] (1000 UTC console, 1600 UTC Epic, 1800 UTC Steam)

[h2]NEW Locomotive: DB BR 111 [/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/eb4f99d502653290750814ed2c29867ef716152a.jpg[/img]

It’s back to all-electric services for our next German route Add-on, representing the early 2010s through rural hilly backdrops and the heart of one of Austria’s biggest cities. Locomotive-hauled Deutsche Bahn regional services make up the bulk of traffic. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/315e4641a28d37e36520eb0e0e582d243835edbd.jpg[/img]

A '70s classic comes to Train Sim World for the first time in the form of the mighty DB BR 111 in DB red livery. These versatile locomotives, built between 1974 and 1984, have seen action all across Germany in the past with some examples running S-Bahn services and others hauling InterCity trains. Despite their age, most of the fleet remains in service today.

The 111 utilises a tap changer control system with both manual and semi-automatic input, bringing a different style of operation to that seen on contemporary locomotives. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/3cc2ae5c1e24af2fc7f697897a863ea7d03af1e1.jpg[/img]

This popular addition to Train Sim World will run services along the length of the route hauling DB Gen 4 Dosto coaches, but will no doubt see action elsewhere in Free Roam for players that have other German routes in their collection. 

[h2]The Route: Salzburg – Rosenheim[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/bbaa287cfb0df572253afeb08393331431462019.jpg[/img]

Continuing the cross-border theme of other Train Sim World 4 routes like S-Bahn Vorarlberg and Berninalinie, this route Add-on, though mostly on German rails, crosses over into Austria at Freilassing and heads into Salzburg Hbf. This important city was the birthplace of Mozart and used during the filming of [i][b]The Sound Of Music[/b][/i] in the 1960s. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/1752fdc9338f8dbd233b3e4e3ad109b23f8186e4.jpg[/img]

With a history spanning over 160 years, the Rosenheim - Salzburg railway has long been a line of vital importance between Germany and Austria. Originally envisaged as early as 1828, it took many years of theorising, designing, and funding to construct. Today, the line is a key corridor for all manners of traffic and has been subject to constant improvements over the decades. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/e668e6b7d4df158dce32def5fe37f821c6acb100.jpg[/img]

Along the route, the scenic countryside delights drivers and passengers alike with sights of the Bavaria region, including the area around the Chiemsee lake. Thirteen stations over 89km of track include towns and villages in the Bavarian hills, such as Übersee, Bernau am Chiemsee and Teisendorf.

[h2]Services and Gameplay[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/e9130d07346fc2b5d30295b6a8814b851c1c525e.jpg[/img]

We’ll talk more on services and gameplay closer to the release, but the inclusion of the ÖBB 4024 from S-Bahn Vorarlberg at the Austrian end of the line and the DB BR 185.2 for freight services, bring with them different ways of experiencing the route.

There will also be added service layers for those that own some existing German route and loco Add-ons. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/75dc21f4c8eb8dc471b472bf585cb8fbba2a613f.jpg[/img]

[b]Train Sim World 4: Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim[/b] route Add-on will be available from 27th February for €35.99/£29.99/$39.99 

[i][b]Steam players will be able to pre-order from 1800 UTC 20th February with a 10% discount.[/b][/i]

Join the Railfan TV team on [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/RailSimulatorDotCom]YouTube[/url] and [url=https://www.twitch.tv/trainsimworldofficial]Twitch[/url] on Thursday 22nd February at 1900 UTC for a preview of Bahnstrecke Salzburg – Rosenheim.

Find out more about Train Sim World 4 by following @trainsimworld on [url=https://twitter.com/trainsimworld]X/Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/trainsim/]Instagram[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/trainsimworld/]Facebook[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/user/RailSimulatorDotCom]YouTube[/url], [url=https://www.twitch.tv/trainsimworldofficial]Twitch[/url], and [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@trainsimworldofficial]TikTok[/url].

[b]Images displayed in this article may depict content that is still in development. The licensed brands may not have been approved by their respective owner and some artwork may still be pending approval.[/b]

notes.title: Train Sim World Roadmap: February 2024
notes.content:
Whew! For those of you who have just joined us from Dovetail Direct: Spring 2024, welcome aboard. We hoped you enjoyed our whistle-stop tour of what you can expect over the next few months. And boy was that a lot of new stuff for you to get excited about, including a new country coming to Train Sim World!

And that will be the focus of February’s Roadmap, too. If you haven’t watched the Direct video, you can do so below - much of what we’ll be covering will be related to it.

In case you missed the live event, catch up on our [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ARYsxeg9x3U][b]Dovetail Direct: Spring 2024 event![/b][/url]

[previewyoutube=ARYsxeg9x3U;full][/previewyoutube]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/60d045378affa1110e00e19321e8675c88c7493a.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]TL;DR (too long; didn’t read) Summary[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] Lots of new content coming to Train Sim World 4!
[*] [b]From Dovetail Games:[/b]
[*] London Overground: Gospel Oak – Barking Riverside
[*] Bahnstrecke Salzburg-Rosenheim
[*] San Bernardino Line: Los Angeles – San Bernardino
[*] As-yet-unnamed upcoming U.S. route
[*] Semmeringbahn: Wiener Neustadt - Mürzzuschlag
[*] [b]From our Partner Programme:[/b]
[*] Simtrack Studios - BR Class 104 & Peak Forest Expansion Pack
[*] Skyhook Games - Cargo Line Vol 2: Aggregates
[*] Rivet Games - Fife Circle Line: Edinburgh - Markinch via Dunfermline & Kirkcaldy
[*] Union Workshop - Tadami Line: AizuWakamatsu – Tadami Our first TSW Japanese route!
[*] [b]More Partners signed up to the Train Sim World Partner Programme[/b]
[*] [b]Core update launched earlier this week[/b] - featuring lots of improvements across the game
[*] [b]Formation Designer beta[/b] - live for Steam and Epic players
[*] [b]West Somerset Railway Remastered[/b] - out now is still 80% off until Monday on Steam!
[/list]

[h3][b]So… About That ‘US Route’[/b][/h3]
Before we get into other content, we wanted to address the (American) elephant in the room.
We do have another US route currently in the works, which is well into development, currently in the ‘No Release Date’ category. We're still working with the licensor on approvals, and when we have them, we'll share more details with you.

Eagle-eyed players may have noticed some clues though recently as to what it may be!

[h2][b]Dovetail Direct: Spring 2024 Summary[/b][/h2]

[h3][b]London Overground: Gospel Oak - Barking Riverside[/b][/h3]

An Aventra Adventure awaits! Discover North & East London boroughs aboard modern traction, traversing a newly electrified and extended line fit for future service.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/5633066e391c89cb405472a38143ca0192fa3bc8.jpg[/img]

Discover the dense North & East London boroughs aboard modern traction, traversing a newly electrified and extended line fit for future riverside service.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/cbc61054a5877a494d05db400df9794139ee35fe.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Bahnstrecke Salzburg-Rosenheim[/b][/h3]

Teased all the way back in our Train Sim World 4 announcement, our latest German route with an Austrian border crossing will be Bahnstrecke Salzburg-Rosenheim!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/75dc21f4c8eb8dc471b472bf585cb8fbba2a613f.jpg[/img]

Discover a scenic and lengthy hilly countryside as you drive across 89km of track operating the DB BR 111 electric loco which utilises a tap changer control system with both manual and semi-automatic input.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/bbaa287cfb0df572253afeb08393331431462019.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]San Bernardino Line: Los Angeles - San Bernardino[/b][/h3]

For our US audience, let’s talk more about the second Metrolink route we’re developing after Antelope Valley…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/6effb6b75750cc4297a019e86d454dd47c654bcd.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/9250a6c0193b7955ba2d18ab7a0c83cffe9a696d.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Semmeringbahn: Wiener Neustadt – Mürzzuschlag[/b][/h3]

Brace yourself for steep challenging gradients, spectacular views, and a mix of tunnels and viaducts!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/3eaa6a8b3250e54daa10d03f3b09ee7e38f07566.jpg[/img]

Displayed on the route map below, you will enjoy a mix of experiences as you switch between ascending winding mountainous terrain, to entering a flatter and faster “racetrack” style of driving as you pass through 17 stations across Semmeringbahn.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/232e3542a256dcc1434edc7c6d703339556d94a7.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/ca0eb37f26a35b3fcfa206ef959f9ba7310ac8bd.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/be0e648ce3e1b18b6772cbfbce71f5159f8e6cad.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Simtrack Studios - BR Class 104 & Peak Forest Expansion Pack[/b][/h3]

Coming from our partners are Simtrack, included in this pack will be the BR Green Class 104 and a timetable upgrade for Peak Forest, with extensions and additional features alongside two new wagons: the 21T Hopper and Covhop wagon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/81975ac0390fe8813fe29ff66b7263f6750045dd.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Skyhook Games - Cargo Line Vol 2: Aggregates[/b][/h3]

Following on from their original Cargo Line pack, Skyhook Games are coming back with the Aggregates pack including the HOA Aggregate Wagon as well as adding new scenarios to both Midland Main Line and Great Western Express add-ons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/4a90a1052740d86da1ce9c793723ddb2b59dedc5.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/a6cc14d4cdcab7c31c6dd149693361f5de7a6f2f.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Rivet Games - Fife Circle Line: Edinburgh - Markinch via Dunfermline & Kirkcaldy and Skyhook Games - ScotRail BR Class 158 DMU[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/1646b34d1043a86443c3fa208cf3772d36087785.jpg[/img]

Rivet Games is taking us to the Fife Circle Line with the Class 170 DMU! This route will include the stunning Fourth Rail bridge, and additionally collaborating alongside Skyhook Games to add the Scotrail BR Class 158 DMU to your collections!

We’re excited to show you more of this route when we’re ready.

[h3][b]Union Workshop - Tadami Line: AizuWakamatsu – Tadami[/b][/h3]

Train Sim World is heading to Japan! As a debut into TSW, Union Workshop have some very early development screenshots for their Tadami Line route!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/77c001dee2f6310beceaba65fee5fb9c724c9696.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/dca2c27168fcb7ce11c00278dd399cd2deba9a02.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/9c5e37275c0869c08678e27a29ad6ae659f687d7.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]Additional Third-Party Partner Developments[/b][/h3]
Alongside our announcements above, we wanted to share a list of the partners we’re currently working alongside for upcoming TSW content, including both existing partners, as well as brand new names to the TSW franchise!
[list]
[*] Rivet Games
[*] Skyhook Games
[*] SimTrack
[*] Luminaries
[*] Alan Thomson Sim
[*] JustTrains
[*] RailTraction
[*] Train-Motion
[*] TrainSim Germany
[*] Union Workshop
[*] Ticket to the North
[*] Halycon Media
[*] RSSLO
[/list]

[h3][b]Tuesday 13th February – 19:00 UTC - Live Roadmap Q&A[/b][/h3]
As a reminder, we didn’t have a Roadmap stream this month with the Dovetail Direct taking its place, so we’ll be live Tuesday evening to talk about the new TSW4 announcements above and to answer your questions across any other areas you’ll want to hear more about. Be sure to submit your questions in advance on our [url=https://forums.dovetailgames.com/threads/february-roadmap-q-a-tuesday-feb-13th.78632/][b]Latest Q&A thread.[/b][/url]

And that’s it! Quite enough excitement for a Sunday evening, we hope you’ll agree. We’ll catch you live on Tuesday to answer your questions, and we hope you’re as excited for the next few months of content as we are!

[h3][b]Dovetail Direct: Spring 2024 Summary[/b][/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/e17763271128225144a8bc7a952d27901ba4bb7c.jpg[/img]

Find out more about Train Sim World 4 by following @trainsimworld on [b][url=https://twitter.com/trainsimworld]Twitter[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.instagram.com/trainsim/]Instagram[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.facebook.com/trainsimworld]Facebook[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.youtube.com/user/RailSimulatorDotCom]YouTube[/url][/b], [b][url=https://www.twitch.tv/trainsimworldofficial]Twitch[/url][/b], and [b][url=https://www.tiktok.com/@trainsimworldofficial]TikTok[/url][/b].

notes.title: Winter Core Update - February
notes.content:
Hello folks, and welcome to February. 
The days are getting longer, spring is around the corner, and – perhaps most excitingly of all – we have a wide range of improvements and quality of life changes releasing today as part of a large core update, which includes an Open Beta for Formation Designer for Steam players. 
You can expect to see improvements for Blackpool Branches, Maintalbahn, Centro Regional Railway Class 323, and many more!

Get a cup of your favourite beverage, because this is a long read.


[h1]Core [/h1]

[list]
[*] Mods created for Add-ons now work in the same way that Core mods do.   
[*] General improvement to brightness on PIS screens to be more visible/readable during both day and night. 
[*] Fixed an issue where service names would extend outside of the Debriefing UI screens 
[*] Fixed an issue where medals for completed Timetables, Scenarios, and Training modules didn’t display correctly on the main menu. 
[*] Fixes to Journey Mode continue option so that the option is consistently offered and works as intended. 
[*] Fixed a crash with Xbox S/X on Scenario Planner with multiple add-ons installed 
[*] Resuming a saved game using Classic Controls will no longer lock the screen. 
[*] Minor memory performance improvements.  
[*] Minor core performance improvements to slightly improve boot time and maintain stability, especially when in large freight yards and on larger routes. 
[*] Various NPC passenger model improvements and fixes. 
[*] Various localisation changes. 
[/list]

[h3]Minimal HUD [/h3]

[list]
[*] Added option to disable Traction Lock icon 
[*] The Clock will now correctly be visible when standing 
[*] Minimal Hud will no longer display 44kmh before actual gameplay starts 
[/list]

[h3]Photo Mode [/h3]

[list]
[*] Added autofocus toggle 
[*] Fixed various issues with camera collisions when orbiting. 
[/list]

[h3]Free Roam [/h3]

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with the SD70ACe display screens so that the brakes can be cut in correctly, allowing the loco to be started. 
[*] Fixed an issue preventing the MRCE and Dispolok 182 from moving. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the DB BR 185.5 wouldn’t move after spawning. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the Class 47 and 52 wouldn’t take power after spawning. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the BR 146 wouldn’t take power after spawning. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the BR 182, 185, 187 wouldn’t take power after spawning. 
[*] Fixed an issue on the Bakerloo Line where players were unable to set destination path for the full length of the route. 
[/list]

[h3]Livery Designer [/h3]

[list]
[*] Improvement to ensure created liveries are appearing correctly in gameplay 
[*] Fixed an issue with the loco model not appearing when copying liveries. 
[*] Fixed an issue where deleted liveries would continue to appear in UI options 
[/list]

[h3]Scoring[/h3]

[list]
[*] Adjustments to scoring thresholds to make achieving a Platinum medal possible across many services and scenarios, and more in line with expectations (90% of maximum possible score). 
[*] Added player assist notification to alert what systems need to be turned on to award the safety system bonus. 
[*] Fixed an issue on the Scoring Breakdown where the added score was inconsistent to the total score awarded. 
[*] Fixed an issue where the speeding penalty was not being correctly applied. 
[*] Fixed an issue where activating Safety systems mid way through a route would award 0 points in the scoring breakdown. 
[*] Fixed an issue where wiper penalties were being applied without it raining due to weather settings. 
[/list]
 

[h3]Known Scoring Issues [/h3]

[i]We are aware of some existing issues with scoring which we intended to resolve in this patch but weren’t able to include, so we’d like to highlight these for you:[/i]

[list]
[*] Antelope Valley ‘EMD F125 Training Introduction’ – Unable to achieve platinum 
[*] Vorarlberg 'Pick Up' scenario – Unable to achieve platinum 
[*] Antelope Valley (Services/Scenarios) – Too easy to achieve platinum without safety systems enabled 
[*] Maintalbahn 'Getting the Cold Shoulder' scenario – Too easy to achieve platinum without safety systems enabled 
[*] [PS4] Score for using safety systems is set to 0 if you enable them after starting a scenario 
[/list]
 
 

[h1]Blackpool Branches [/h1]

[list]
[*] Passengers no longer appear at Lichfield Trent Valley in the scenario "Engineering a Shunt", as this station has engineering work going on. 
[*] Moved markers at Salwick Goods Loop to be more forgiving to players 
[*] Moved stop location at Blackpool North to accomodate longer locomotives 
[*] Fixes timing errors on services 2J56, 2J54 and 2J52 where instructions were an hour early 
[*] Fixes to locomotives spawning in buffers if they were too long which caused derailments in multiple services 
[*] Made the Class 31 drivable on the 3-coach-consist and the Mineral wagons on freight services 
[*] Fixed Numbering so each class 142 livery displays correct numbers for the era 
[*] Fixed an issue where Service 2J52 would cause a derailment upon launch.
[/list] 

[h3]Class 142 [/h3]

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with AI getting stuck trying to open doors 
[*] Implemented a manual Gear Hold switch in the cab of the 142 
[/list]

[h3]Class 47 [/h3]

[list]
[*] Changed font on vehicle numbering to the correct type 
[*] Fixed an issue on the Class 47 service 0Z25 where the player spawns at a faraway station 
[/list]

 

[h1]Midland Main Line [/h1]

[list]
[*] Fixed various spelling mistakes on signage and in text. 
[*] Reduced number of high-rise buildings around Loughborough, Long Eaton and Derby stations to better represent the area. 
[*] Removed a signal box from a yard behind Spondon station. 
[*] Fixed various posters at Derby station to resolve flickering textures. 
[/list]

[h3]Class 158 [/h3]

[list]
[*] Gangways and cab/gangway doors will now behave as expected on 4-car formations. 
[/list]



[h1]Bernina Line [/h1]

[list]
[*] Adjustments to fog variables to improve visuals and fine-tunability to fit the scenery better.  
(Valleys will have less dense fog, hills will have more dense fog) 
[*] Carriages coupled behind Allegra EMU will correctly have new rain effects on the windows. 
[*] Passengers should now be lit by the interior passenger lights 
[/list]
 


[h1]Birmingham Cross City [/h1]

[list]
[*] Fixed no passengers spawning at Kings Norton or Gravelly Hill. 
[*] Fixed an issue where Kings Norton and Lichfield City didn’t show on the PIS 
[/list]

[h3]WMR Class 323 [/h3]

[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with headlight emissions 
[/list]

[h3]EWS Class 66 [/h3]

[list]
[*] Tweaks to textures (Exterior body made redder, window glass glare reduced, and head/tail/marker bulb textures made more yellow tinted) 
[/list]

 

[h1]Centro Regional Railway Class 323 [/h1]

[list]
[*] AWS and DVD audio now plays out of the PlayStation controller. 
[*] Fixed duplicate Journey Mode services. 
[*] Player can now interact with the MCBs in the PTS.  
[*] Player can now interact with the guard panels in the PTS. 
[*] Fixed a crash while loading the 'Misty Morning Start' scenario 
[*] Corrected introduction text on the 'Misty Morning Start' scenario 
[*] Fix incorrect AI headlight setup on the ‘Regional Rescue’ scenario when the player passes an AI service at 12:09. 
[*] Fixed assets with no texture in the "Engineering a Shunt" scenario 
[*] Fixed destination marker to correctly display ‘Four Oaks’ on the ‘Regional Speed Restriction’ scenario. 
[*] Fixed an issue causing text messages to appear in the wrong location on the ‘Regional Speed Restriction’ scenario. 
[*] Fixed Four Oaks unloading not completing when late, and tail lights being on for the player consist.

[url=https://live.dovetailgames.com/live/train-sim-world/articles/article/tsw4-wsr-remastered][b]You can read all the details, including a deep dive of the new timetable in our dedicated article[/b][/url] or watch the livestream tonight at 19:00 UTC on YouTube and Twitch with Matt, Joe and Liam.

[h3][b]Winter Core Update – the next release[/b][/h3]

If you read this morning’s West Somerset Railway article, you’ll have seen we’ve also let you know a little more about what’s happening with the next part of our Winter Core update, which is due next week.

We’ll provide a full Patch Notes list with the update, but to whet your collective whistles, here are some highlights which we’re currently testing and hope to release:
[list]
[*] Improved PIS Brightness for more visibility and readability in day/night
[*] Multiple Free Roam fixes for locos that weren’t able to move after spawning
[*] Scoring adjustments so achieving a Platinum medal is more in line with expectations
[*] Added option to disable Traction Lock icon in the Minimal HUD
[/list]

[h3][b]Formation Designer – Open Beta[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/c04c676ec7b8d8e3aea4633f73b2d03194775f7e.jpg[/img]

Alongside next week’s update, we’ll be offering Steam players the opportunity to try out and feed back on perhaps the most exciting of our upcoming Core updates, Formation Designer. However, we’ll be doing it a little differently to normal.

Formation Designer will allow you to assemble your own consists and formations for use in Scenario Planner and Free roam. This will increase customisation options to create the perfect Scenario and remove the need to spawn different preset formations into the world and rearrange them manually (although that can be quite fun in itself). In its final release, Formation Designer will also allow for your created consists and combinations to be shared via Creators Club, similar to Livery Designer and Scenario Planner.

Because of the sheer number of permutations and options players will be able to combine, testing every possible option is very challenging – so, rather than hold the update any longer, we’re looking for your help. We’ll open up a bespoke feedback forum with details on how you can get involved with the beta, and you can let us know what you think. What you enjoy, what you don’t enjoy, any issues you encounter and any combinations of rolling stock which are proving challenging. Please note: this beta is only available for Steam players. For players of other platforms, we’ll release Formation Designer when we’ve had a chance to review initial beta feedback, and we’re happy it’s ready.

We want it to be a cornerstone of player creativity going forward, so want to bring you into the fold as we shape it up for full release. More details to come next week, but we thank you all in advance – we can’t wait to see what you think!

notes.title: West Somerset Railway: Remastered – Out Now!
notes.content:
A free upgrade is available to all Train Sim World 4 players that own the West Somerset Railway route Add-on! New scenery, a short boundary extension, TSW4 features and a whole new timetable give England’s longest heritage railway a new lease of life!

We’ve also got an update for you on the forthcoming second part of the Winter Core Update. If you want to skip ahead, this is found at the bottom of this article.

[h3][b]West Somerset Railway: Remastered[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/e199bef02f78cfdf659ecf5e25d1ac8636cd5e7d.jpg[/img]

The remastering of this route comes as a result of the passion and enthusiasm of our Development Team, with much of the work being done by Game Designer Liam. The work involved has resulted in this route Add-on from a few years ago being brought fully up to Train Sim World 4 standards, including the following:
[list]
[*] [b]TOD4 Lighting and Dynamic Weather[/b]
[*] [b]Volumetric Fog[/b] and [b]Chained Paths[/b] in Scenario Planner
[*] [b]Scenery Updates[/b], including Minehead town, Watchet Harbour and the yard at Bishops Lydeard
[*] [b]Audio improvements[/b] to the route, Class 47, Class 09 and Class 33 and Class 52 loco Add-ons
[*] [b]Short extension[/b] to the track scenery at Norton Fitzwarren to include part of the Bristol – Exeter Main Line for AI traffic.
[*] [b]Coal loading, functioning water towers[/b] and [b]AI whistling[/b] at whistle board locations.
[*] [b]A new, additional timetable[/b] based on the real-world gala timetable from 2022 allowing for steam services, shuttles, winter specials and rail tours for players with relevant Add-ons.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/6a323ba7e4bc19849a7d870e6bc03b5dbfac1ccf.jpg[/img]

The results will see this popular route tie into a host of Add-ons from the wider Train Sim World back catalogue, including more recent releases like the Flying Scotsman loco Add-on. A full break down of additional layers and the specific services they add to the new timetable can be found further down in this article.

The new steam gala timetable pivots mainly around the Peak Forest Railway route Add-on and the addition of Jubilee, 8F and 4F steam locomotives, all of which have visited the real-world railway in recent years. Coal loading is functional at Minehead Station (players can pull into a designated spot, where coal will automatically load) as are existing water towers and a newly modelled one at Bishops Lydeard.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/e027f8f3d0c039c5c6f45919a7215ef906a30965.jpg[/img]

Even for those playing the native route with the preserved Class 47 and Class 09 in the existing timetable can enjoy the upgraded visual features whilst operating heritage trains between Bishops Lydeard and the seaside town of Minehead, with shunting moves at either end of the line.

There are also some audio improvements, from the locomotives themselves and their reaction to the environment (under bridges for example), to the sounds made when finding collectibles and the rain hitting canopies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/a43901612efb56bf65863749ac99c70a3d436e0e.jpg[/img]

Both Class 33 and Class 52 loco Add-ons (available separately) also get a refresh, with the new Train Sim World 4 rain effects implemented on the windscreens and audio improvements to their horns. These then layer into the original timetable. The West Somerset Railway route Add-on is required to make use of these loco Add-ons.

[previewyoutube=Hwt5_Ok3-24;full][/previewyoutube]

If you want learn more about the upgrades and content, the remastering process and get an insight into the real-world West Somerset Railway, join Matt, Liam and Joe for tonight’s livestream at 1900 UTC on YouTube and Twitch where they’ll be showcasing the West Somerset Railway: Remastered route Add-on to kick off the Festival of Rail!

Train Sim World 4: West Somerset Railway: Remastered route Add-on is available now for Xbox One, 
Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Epic Games Store, and Steam for £19.99/€24.99/$24.99.

Train Sim World Compatible: Peak Forest Railway route Add-on is available for £29.99/$39.99/€35.99

Train Sim World Compatible Class 33 / Class 52 Loco Add-ons are available for £11.99/$19.99/€13.99

Scroll down for a full list of content required for playable and AI service layers.

[h3][b]Timetable and Layers Deep Dive[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/2a0454d95b5f2d67de0ebfc8fd4aae7b809f512f.jpg[/img]

The updated layering, timetable and environment for the West Somerset Railway route Add-on takes much of its inspiration from the real-world railway and the various guests and unusual operations that it has seen in recent years.

[h3][b]Railway Galas – Events for Enthusiasts[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/a789207df1fb62871f913771fec27d57f749645d.jpg[/img]

Railways Galas have run on heritage railways since their first appearance following branch line closures in the 1960s and 70s. Often these events were celebratory occasions run by volunteers and locals without much need for profit or visitor attendance. Today however they form vital parts of the events calendar and with 20 miles of track to play with, the West Somerset Railway takes great pride in hosting two or three per year, normally themed around steam or diesel traction.

Both the original and new timetables represent diesel and steam gala operations, with the latter hosting full length runs, shuttles, visits to Norton Fitzwarren (not normally visited by service trains) and freight moves! This is based on the real-world gala timetable from 2022.

[h3][b]Steam Locomotives (Playable Layers)[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/d8dded7a9ed8fdf0233d66d2a355c84978c9d1f3.jpg[/img]

Today, the real-world WSR is known primarily as a tourist steam railway. As a result, the new timetable layers in three steam locomotives from the Peak Forest Railway route Add-on as well as the iconic National Railway Museum locomotive: LNER Class A3 60103 Flying Scotsman, available as a loco Add-on or as part of Train Sim World 4: Deluxe Edition.

Flying Scotsman last visited the WSR in 2017, providing one of the busiest events ever held in the railway’s history. Every seat on the trains that it hauled along the line were full and last minute ‘no shows’ quickly had their seats taken up by those on a last-minute waiting list! Photographers and railfans lined the lineside and a commemorative booklet was produced documenting the occasion. The locomotive does make occasional appearances on rail tours down in Devon and Cornwall, running along the stretch of main line past Norton Fitzwarren on its way there and back.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/6a969b54ba070f0d100aa869201210f265516d64.jpg[/img]

Similarly, main line LMS Jubilee locomotives often visit the line during rail tours, with loco swaps occurring at Bishops Lydeard. No.45596 visited as recently as 2023, with others making an appearance on the line in 2021 and 2016.

2016 also saw an LMS 8F visit the line in the form of no.48624 for that year’s Spring Steam Gala. This included some double-headed trains with other visiting locomotives.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/be43a1395ce94cbe3fecb068777de57b18ab5649.jpg[/img]

Players that have completed the Tier 2 Mastery Challenges on the West Somerset Railway will have seen an LMS 4F scenery tile being unloaded at Dunster Station. Now, this locomotive can form part of the timetable, recreating the occasions that no.44422 visited the railway in 2006, 2016 and 2017.

Steam services also form the backbone of the Winter Specials and Santa Trains that make up a crucial part of heritage railways’ business in the ‘off’ season and players that own the West Cornwall Steam Railtour Add-on will be able to recreate those, complete with festive lights and music!

[h3][b]Class 150 (Playable Shuttle Services)[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/1d14fa8bdf47152bc026017b3b70b6f274cc2dfa.jpg[/img]

The West Cornwall Local route Add-on allows for the running of Class 150 shuttles from off the map at Taunton, through Norton Fitzwarren to Bishops Lydeard. This important main line connection has run shuttles over many years, including the 1992 GWR 150 celebrations. More recently, a full trial of services was run in the summer of 2019 with the hope of one day justifying regular connections to Taunton in the future.

[h3][b]HSTs (AI and Free Roam)[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/f9fe67f0ac9b43b63e956cb63801c735c6a1741f.jpg[/img]

Great Western Express owners will see AI services running along the stretch of main line at Norton Fitzwarren, as was the case during the route Add-on's era of 2017 / 2018. Today these are more often run by more modern IETs, but GWR HSTs have run the length of the WSR as recently as 2023, when the operator was required to store them at Minehead. Players can recreate their running between Norton Fitzwarren and Minehead in Free Roam.

[h3][b]Class 66 Movements (AI and Free Roam)[/b][/h3]

Despite being a heritage railway, the connection to the main line at Norton Fitzwarren facilitates a number of different freight moves by other operators, including regular ballast cleaning trains that use the Norton Triangle to the benefit of the WSR. These are almost exclusively run by Class 66 locomotives, which have also appeared on the line to haul specials, such as one at a 2016 event hosted by model railway company PECO.

Players with any of the Class 66 Add-ons (Southeastern Highspeed, East Coast Main Line, Great Western Express, Engineering Express Pack) can make use of this locomotive in Free Roam mode. Southeastern Highspeed and the RHTT Add-ons result in AI / static stock appearing.

[h3][b]Additional DMU Running (Original Timetable Layers + Free Roam Options)[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/3e3da5b9ddd9db5a92cb9c89cb8e39469337ef4a.jpg[/img]

Though the Class 101 has never ventured onto WSR rails, players with Northern Trans-Pennine or Tees Valley Line can enjoy using this DMU in the original timetable to represent 3-car services that run during events. In reality, these are run by the similar Class 115.

Midland Main Line players may also wish to use the EMT Class 158 in Free Roam to recreate the Class 158 rail tours and charters that have used the WSR over the years, including some in the mid-2000s SWT livery that was very similar to that of EMT’s.

And for some fun (but non-prototypical) running, those with Blackpool Branches can see what a visiting Class 142 Pacer would do along the line in Free Roam. Pacers used to be seen on the main line stretch of track at Norton Fitzwarren running down to Devon but have not yet run onto WSR rails.

Blackpool Branches also allows players to run different liveries of the Class 47, including specific, named examples.

[h3][b]Diesel Gala (Original Timetable Layers + Free Roam Options)[/b][/h3]

[b]Class 08, 09, 20, 31, 33, 37, 40, 45, 47, 52 and 66 Locomotives[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/e70975d78c0044127a9cf5b5a0f549ddace4758d.jpg[/img]

The original West Somerset Railway timetable makes plenty of use of the diesel locomotives available from other Train Sim World releases to create a real mixed bag of visitors for the in-game gala experience. The Class 47, Class 33 and Class 52 represent the WSR’s home fleet from circa 2017 / 2018, owned and run by the DEPG (Diesel Electric Preservation Group) whereas the 09 represents the WSR’s Bishops Lydeard-based shunter, which occasionally sees action at Minehead too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/cfa4be9bc0e9024af12f2199eb23bce83fa056c3.jpg[/img]

Beyond this, services can be run with substituted locomotives from other route and loco Add-ons, all of which have seen action on the line at Diesel Galas over the years. Tandem 20s visited in both 2017 and 2018 whereas a Class 40 and 45 guested during September of 1995 and again in 1997. Class 08 no.08377 was a regular shunter on the line before moving on to another heritage line in 2013 and Class 31s have appeared, like Class 37s, as both guest locomotives and main line visitors in the past. Class 31s also hauled the notable Butlin’s Express services from Bristol Temple Meads to Minehead and have brought departmental test trains to the line between 2012 and 2014.

Whilst only the original timetable still makes use of some of these as playable content, players can use Train Sim World 4’s Free Roam feature to operate them within the new timetable too.

[h2][b]Required Content[/b][/h2]

All of the Compatible Layers that can be implemented into West Somerset Railway: Remastered can be found below. All players require Train Sim World 4 to make use of the upgrades and new timetable.

[b]Playable Layers (in the NEW timetable)[/b]
[list]
[*] West Somerset Railway
[*] Flying Scotsman 
[*] Peak Forest Railway (8F, 4F, Jubilee)
[*] West Cornwall Local (Class 150)
[*] West Cornwall Steam Railtour
[/list]

[b]Playable & AI Layers (in the ORIGINAL timetable)[/b]
[list]
[*] WSR Class 33
[*] WSR Class 52
[*] Northern Trans-Pennine (Class 101 / 47 / 45)
[*] BR Heavy Freight Pack (Class 40 / 08)
[*] Tees Valley Line (Class 37 / 101)
[*] DSN Class 20
[*] BR Class 31
[/list]

[b]AI Layers (in the NEW timetable)[/b]
[list]
[*] BR Heavy Freight Pack (Class 40 / 08)
[*] Tees Valley Line (Class 37 / 101)
[*] DSN Class 20 
[*] Great Western Express (HST)
[*] Northern Trans-Pennine (Class 101 / 47 / 45)
[*] Rail Operations Group BR Class 37/7 
[*] RHTT 
[*] Southeastern High Speed
[*] WSR Class 33 
[*] WSR Class 52 
[/list]

[b]Optional Content for some Free Roam fun![/b]
[list]
[*] Midland Main Line (Class 158)
[*] Blackpool Branches (Class 142 Pacer + 47 / 08 liveries)
[/list]

[h2][b]Winter Core Update – the next release[/b][/h2]

We hope you all enjoy the new lease of life given to West Somerset Railway, and it’s at this stage we wanted to let you know what’s happening with the next part of our Winter Core update, which is due next week.

We’ll provide a full Patch Notes list with the update, but to whet your collective whistles, here are some highlights which we’re currently testing and hope to release:
[list]
[*] Improved PIS Brightness for more visibility and readability in day/night
[*] Multiple Free Roam fixes for locos that weren’t able to move after spawning
[*] Scoring adjustments so achieving a Platinum medal is more in line with expectations
[*] Added option to disable Traction Lock icon in the Minimal HUD
[/list]

[h2][b]Formation Designer – Open Beta[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/c04c676ec7b8d8e3aea4633f73b2d03194775f7e.jpg[/img]

Alongside next week’s update, we’ll be offering Steam players the opportunity to try out and feed back on perhaps the most exciting of our upcoming Core updates, Formation Designer. However, we’ll be doing it a little differently to normal.

Formation Designer will allow you to assemble your own consists and formations for use in Scenario Planner and Free roam. This will increase customisation options to create the perfect Scenario and remove the need to spawn different preset formations into the world and rearrange them manually (although that can be quite fun in itself). In its final release, Formation Designer will also allow for your created consists and combinations to be share via Creators Club, similar to Livery Designer and Scenario Planner.

Because of the sheer number of permutations and options players will be able to combine, testing every possible option is very challenging – so, rather than hold the update any longer, we’re looking for your help. We’ll open up a bespoke feedback forum with details on how you can get involved with the beta, and you can let us know what you think. What you enjoy, what you don’t enjoy, any issues you encounter and any combinations of rolling stock which are proving challenging. Please note: this beta is only available for Steam players. For players of other platforms, we’ll release Formation Designer when we’ve had a chance to review initial beta feedback, and we’re happy it’s ready.

We want it to be a cornerstone of player creativity going forward, so want to bring you into the fold as we shape it up for full release. More details to come next week, but we thank you all in advance – we can’t wait to see what you think!

notes.title: Edinburgh - Glasgow: Engineering Express Pack - Out Now
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/da80edba34239781ae3c7bc364d224915b6f5f50.jpg[/img]

Rescue Class 385s between Scotland's two major cities and take new Class 66 liveries beyond in Free 
Roam with the Edinburgh - Glasgow: Engineering Express Pack by Rivet Games - Out Now as a Gameplay Pack for the Train Sim World Compatible: ScotRail Express: Edinburgh - Glasgow route Add-on!

[i][b]Steam players get a 10% off until 30th January[/b][/i]

[h3][b]Train Sim World 4: Edinburgh - Glasgow: Engineering Express Pack[/b][/h3]

It’s not all smooth sailing out on the main line, from engineering movements to daring drags. In this pack, explore more gameplay and unique operations on Rivet Games’ ScotRail Express: Edinburgh - Glasgow route Add-on, with newly liveried Class 66s joining ranks alongside the Class 385.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/3ce49300d6091cde7d56bf32544cfc18a78b526a.jpg[/img]

Embark on the task of shifting hefty ballast trains along the Edinburgh - Glasgow line, without causing delays, in preparation for day-to-day engineering works, and face typical Scottish weather as you drag Class 385s on delivery and rescue runs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/7e8d8f502556b2dd2b270fe8a64509c69ca1c8e9.jpg[/img]

A sample of sheds form the traction for these unique duties, resplendent in two brand new liveries! Encompassed in sleek blue, the Class 66 arrives in Direct Rail Services livery, and although not to be ONE-upped, it is accompanied by the pleasing magenta tones of Ocean Network Express livery.

Of course, both can be used in Free Roam across any of the routes in your collection, bringing these new liveries to other parts of the UK rail network.

[previewyoutube=7CIjZed96C0;full][/previewyoutube]

Train Sim World 4 is required and Train Sim World Compatible: ScotRail Express: Edinburgh - Glasgow is recommended to make use of this gameplay pack.

Train Sim World 4: Edinburgh - Glasgow: Engineering Express Pack is out nowfor Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Epic Games Store, and Steam. It is available for £9.99*/€11.99/$14.99
*£9.49 on the PlayStation Store (EU / USD prices on PS remain as above).

[h3][b]The Route[/b][/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2386156/Train_Sim_World_4_Compatible_ScotRail_Express_Edinburgh__Glasgow_Route_AddOn/

[previewyoutube=-Tt7UvWV6jo;full][/previewyoutube]

If you’ve yet to take the modern Class 385 between Scotland’s two more prominent cities, then there’s plenty of passenger action to take on as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/58f648a766a57f3b327001046dcc23f7c95a5358.jpg[/img]

Both the route and traction for this busy Scottish commuter route come with a selection of features new to Train Sim World. For the first time a working TMS (Train Management System) screen provides the player with new and relevant information on the unit, as well as interactive functions, including the long-awaited arrival of PIS announcements!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/57e02bbda6d481c91f4a7dab1e58bf7a5e1979a0.jpg[/img]

Across the route, the scenery and environment changes between the built-up urban and suburban landscapes of both Edinburgh and Glasgow, with abundant greenery and rolling countryside occupying much of the space between them.

Train Sim World Compatible: ScotRail Express: Edinburgh – Glasgow is available for Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Epic Games Store, and Steam for £29.99/$39.99/€35.99

Screenshots show the route Add-on with the additional Gameplay Pack installed.

notes.title: Berninalinie: Tirano - Ospizio Bernina – Out Now!
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=1MhdUuDzKxo;full][/previewyoutube]

It’s time to head across the border and up the mountain! Berninalinie: Tirano - Ospizio Bernina, by Rivet Games, is out now featuring the ABe 8/12 Allegra EMU.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2584110/Train_Sim_World_4_Berninalinie_Tirano__Ospizio_Bernina_Route_AddOn/

[h3][b]Berninalinie Manual[/b][/h3]
Read the [url=https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/2584110/manuals/TrainSimWorld4_BerninaLine-OspizioBernina-Tirano_Manual-PC_EN_v4.pdf?t=1705398119][b]Berninalinie Player Manual[/b][/url] by Rivet Games

[h3][b]New Narrow-Gauge Route[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/6e91a5e1deb3afc4bb2523775c6eba0513ff3c56.jpg[/img]

Once again, Train Sim World introduces Swiss Narrow-Gauge to a route Add-on after the previously released Arosalinie, also by Rivet Games. This picturesque tourist railway from the early 1900s winds its metre-gauge track out from the Italian town of Tirano over some impressive railway infrastructure including the stunning Brusio Viaduct and tunnels carved straight through the mountainous terrain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/fddb8fdf1e21f41cb2431c217ea3f1a611f0877c.jpg[/img]

The natural landscape is just as eye-catching, with a number of unique elements and assets included in-game to bring the geography of Berninalinie to life. A seasonally frozen lake at Lago Bianco appears depending on the time of year that timetable mode is set in, as does a unique glacier at Alp Grüm some 2091m above sea level, all made more dramatic with the dynamic weather and fog that form part of the Train Sim World 4 experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/2c0b217b4187215af6ea2d33cca8174862dc2ec3.jpg[/img]

Inquisitive players may also want to take a wander and explore the landscape up close! Alp Grüm features a viewing balcony that can be admired on foot and the Lake at Miralago Station can be walked around too. Completion of the Mastery Challenges will yield something else to admire in the scenery representative of the unique challenge that local farmers encounter when their cattle require medical attention!

[h3][b]The ABe 8/12 Allegra EMU[/b][/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/d68db9d145f8412056e02707ea2f88c0cf0a5487.jpg[/img]

The record-holding ABe 8/12 Allegra EMU, operated by the Rhaetian Railway or RhB brings modern electric traction to this century-old route. Its dual voltage feature means that players with the Arosalinie route Add-on can switch pantographs and operate it there in Free Roam alongside the Ge 4/4 II. On Berninalinie, the unit tackles both the curves and gradients with ease, whilst doing its best not to disturb the sensitive snow – its inclusion of a whistle, rather than a horn, is to prevent the risk of avalanche!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/0b3ce70587e05f8a423cd83a6df6b0c51c693ee1.jpg[/img]

Audible announcements are also implemented in three languages: English, Italian and German and cycle automatically building on the feature seen in the Edinburgh – Glasgow route Add-on, also by Rivet Games.

Also included in this route Add-on is a selection of additional rolling stock to allow for the running of mixed consists behind the Allegra:
[list]
[*] RhB ZA Tank Wagon
[*] RhB SP-W Timber Wagon
[*] EW-1 A and B coaches
[/list]

[previewyoutube=ocwP5ublPxg;full][/previewyoutube]

The service timetable consists of passenger services running the full length of the route between Tirano and Ospizio Bernina. Along the way, some trains will pick up additional stock such as the Tank or Timber Wagons, making for some unique operations with EMU-hauled freight. There are 49 services in total, with six half-way services from either Tirano or Ospizio Bernina to Poschiavo, where shunting moves can be operated in the morning.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/1840bd35e0fbec410a8e93082bf7d4af9024c283.jpg[/img]

Three BEX (Bernina Express) services form part of the timetable, consisting of a run up and down with a shunting manoeuvre at Tirano. These trains feature the open-air coach from the RhB Anniversary Collection Add-On for players that own it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44534860/e7250195a18fbd96f0fb1136ad786d31c67691d7.jpg[/img]

Five Scenarios and both new and existing collectibles to find are included to keep players busy along Berninaline and encourage some exploration of this visually impressive route Add-on!

Train Sim World 4: Berninaline: Tirano - Ospizio Bernina route Add-on is available now for [b]€35.99/£29.99/$39.99
[/b]
If you missed the preview stream, you can go back and join Jamie and Alex, plus Jasper from Rivet Games, on Twitch and YouTube for the preview of Train Sim World 4: Berninaline: Tirano - Ospizio Bernina.

[previewyoutube=HjWLnmzIciA;full][/previewyoutube]
